tara: quick idea to speed small fixes during change windows: introduce an "ephemeral rollout" mode in deploy-bot. lightweight, non-persistent routing tweak.

ben: how is ephemeral different from a normal pin?

tara: it doesn't update the canonical pin store. it's routed at the gateway level for a limited window, auto-removed after the window expires or on rollback. think: temporary traffic steering, low overhead.

lee: i like that. we should have strict guards though. limits on percent + window and a dry-run that shows impact.

ci-bot: policy check: ephemeral allowed only for <=15% traffic and windows <=90m unless a change-window is declared.

ben: can you sketch CLI?

tara: sure: ```
# preview the ephemeral plan
deploy-bot ephemeral preview --service frontend --image web:v1.2.4 --percent 10 --window 45m --dry-run

# apply ephemeral rollout
deploy-bot ephemeral apply --service frontend --image web:v1.2.4 --percent 10 --window 45m --note "hotfix 123"
```

lee: nice. dry-run should output a concise JSON blob our tooling can ingest: estimated p50/p95 delta, expected cache-warm percentage, token/cpu cost delta, and a generated ephemeral-id.

ben: +1. auditors will want a clear event pushed to the internal audit topic with ephemeral-id, user, and policy flags.

ops-bot: suggestion: ephemeral actions get an "ephemeral" tag in the release doc; also emit a small human brief for the channel automatically. example: "ephemeral-id e3f9: frontend web:v1.2.4 -> 10% for 45m; auto-revert on anomaly."

lee: rollback ergonomics: single-step revert by id and optional snapshot of current routing metadata.

ben: example revert command?

tara: ```
# revert ephemeral rollout and save notes
deploy-bot ephemeral revert --id e3f9 --snapshot-notes
```

ci-bot: small guard: if an ephemeral rollout is attempted during blackout hours (02:00-04:00 UTC) an explicit --force-override is required and must include an on-call approval tag.

lee: we should also provide templates for on-call: preflight checklist, paste-ready brief, and rollback snippet. storing them as YAML templates in repo release-templates/ephemeral/ seems sensible.

ben: add --template arg to apply so ops can run `--template hotfix-quick` and skip manual flags. templates must still go through dry-run and policy check.

ops-bot: automated monitors: if error rate jumps >4x baseline in the ephemeral cohort for 1 minute, trigger immediate revert and open an incident stub linked to ephemeral-id.

tara: for UX, deploy-bot will return a tiny one-line and a JSON block. one-line for slack, JSON for the console and release doc.

lee: can we also have a small simulator/playground that runs the dry-run math locally without touching infra? helps PMs and SEs validate impact.

ben: will need an audit schema: fields = [ephemeral_id, user, service, image, percent, window, outcome, annotations]. i'll draft and put it in the infra/audit-schemas repo.

ci-bot: reminder: ephemeral mode won't bypass any security scanning or image signing checks. all usual gates apply.

tara: plan of action: 1) lee builds dry-run output shape + simulator 2) ben drafts audit schema + repo templates 3) i'll prototype CLI and bot responses 4) ops will propose monitor thresholds. target: alpha next change window.

ops-bot: note: alpha will run in staging only by default. production path requires opt-in and a feature flag per team.

ben: i'll open PRs for templates and schema today.

lee: i'll put together the simulator script and a sample dry-run JSON.

ci-bot: policy acked. ensure logs include user principal and action reason.

tara: thanks all. this should make tiny hotfixes faster with clear auditability. i'll create the alpha thread when CLI prototype is ready. :rocket:

deploy-bot: preview ready: ephemeral-id=e3f9, estimated p50:+1ms, p95:+8ms, cache-warm: 72%, estimated cost delta:+$0.02/10k requests.
